name: Northern Renaissance
description: While Italy rediscovered ancient Greece and Rome, painters in Flanders, the Netherlands and Germany fell in love with oil paint and tiny details. Their canvases hide whole worlds in a single window, a mirror or a piece of fruit.

artworks.title: The Arnolfini Portsrait
artworks.imageCredit: Jan van Eyck, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
artworks.description: A couple stands in a quiet room, hand in hand. Nothing here is accidental: the single candle, the little dog and the shoes on the floor all carry meaning.
artworks.artistBio: Jan van Eyck was a painter working in Bruges in the 1400s. He perfected the use of oil paint, building up thin glowing layers that made his surfaces shine like jewels.
artworks.funFact: Above the mirror on the back wall he wrote 'Jan van Eyck was here, 1434'. In the mirror you can see two tiny figures entering the room, and one of them may be the painter himself.
